---

This guide will walk you through the process of installing and deploying a smart contract using [js-stellar-sdk](https://github.com/stellar/js-stellar-sdk), the [Python SDK](https://github.com/StellarCN/py-stellar-base), or the [Go SDK](https://github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk). We will cover the setup of a sample Rust contract, creating a Node.js project to manage the deployment, and finally, installing the Wasm of the contract and deploying it to the network

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, ensure you have the following installed:

1. [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org) and Cargo (for compiling smart contracts)
2. [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) and npm (for running JavaScript deployment scripts), [Python](https://www.python.org) 3.10 or later (for running Python deployment scripts), or [Go](https://go.dev/doc/install) 1.25 or later (for running Go deployment scripts)
3. [Stellar CLI](../../smart-contracts/getting-started/setup#install-the-stellar-cli)

## Initialize a sample Rust Contract

```bash
stellar contract init hello-world
cd hello-world
stellar contract build
```

This sequence of commands creates a new directory for your project, initializes a new Soroban smart contract within that directory, and builds the contract. The build generates .wasm file in the path `hello-world/target/wasm32v1-none/release/hello_world.wasm`

## Create a Node Project

1. Create a new directory for your Node.js project and navigate into it:

```bash
mkdir deploy-contract
cd deploy-contract
```

2. Initialize a new Node.js project and install necessary dependencies:

```bash
npm init -y
npm install @stellar/stellar-sdk
```

For Python, skip the Node.js project and install the SDK instead:

```bash
pip install stellar-sdk
```

For Go, create a Go module in the same directory and add the SDK:

```bash
go mod init deploy-contract
go get github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk
```

## Set Up Deployment Scripts

### Imports

Import necessary modules in your script. In JavaScript, save the file as `deploy.mjs` to enable ES module imports. In Go, save it as `main.go`:

<CodeGroup>

```javascript JavaScript
import * as StellarSDK from "@stellar/stellar-sdk";
import fs from "fs";
```

```python Python
from stellar_sdk import Keypair, Network, SorobanServer, TransactionBuilder, scval
from stellar_sdk.soroban_rpc import GetTransactionStatus, SendTransactionStatus
from stellar_sdk.xdr import TransactionMeta
```

```go Go
package main

import (
  "context"
  "crypto/rand"
  "errors"
  "fmt"
  "log"
  "os"
  "time"

  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/keypair"
  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/network"
  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/strkey"
  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/txnbuild"
  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/xdr"

  client "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/clients/rpcclient"
  protocol "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/protocols/rpc"
)
```

</CodeGroup>

### Installing the Wasm on the network

Create a function to upload the compiled Wasm file:

<CodeGroup>

```javascript JavaScript
async function uploadWasm(filePath) {
  const bytecode = fs.readFileSync(filePath);
  const account = await server.getAccount(sourceKeypair.publicKey());
  const operation = StellarSDK.Operation.uploadContractWasm({ wasm: bytecode });
  return await buildAndSendTransaction(account, operation);
}
```

```python Python
def upload_wasm(file_path):
    with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
        bytecode = f.read()
    account = server.load_account(source_keypair.public_key)
    return build_and_send_transaction(
        account, lambda builder: builder.append_upload_contract_wasm_op(bytecode)
    )
```

```go Go
func uploadWasm(ctx context.Context, filePath string) (protocol.GetTransactionResponse, error) {
  bytecode, err := os.ReadFile(filePath)
  if err != nil {
    return protocol.GetTransactionResponse{}, err
  }
  account, err := server.LoadAccount(ctx, sourceKeypair.Address())
  if err != nil {
    return protocol.GetTransactionResponse{}, err
  }
  operation := &txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction{
    HostFunction: xdr.HostFunction{
      Type: xdr.HostFunctionTypeHostFunctionTypeUploadContractWasm,
      Wasm: &bytecode,
    },
    SourceAccount: sourceKeypair.Address(),
  }
  return buildAndSendTransaction(ctx, account, operation)
}
```

</CodeGroup>

This function reads the compiled Wasm file, retrieves account details from the network, and installs the bytecode using `uploadContractWasm` Stellar operation, which when wrapped in a transaction is sent to the network.

### Deploy contract

Deploy the contract by referencing the Wasm hash:

<CodeGroup>

```javascript JavaScript
async function deployContract(response) {
  const account = await server.getAccount(sourceKeypair.publicKey());
  const operation = StellarSDK.Operation.createCustomContract({
    wasmHash: StellarSDK.scValToNative(response.returnValue),
    address: StellarSDK.Address.fromString(sourceKeypair.publicKey()),
  });
  const responseDeploy = await buildAndSendTransaction(account, operation);
  const contractAddress = StellarSDK.scValToNative(responseDeploy.returnValue);
  console.log(contractAddress);
}
```

```python Python
def deploy_contract(response):
    account = server.load_account(source_keypair.public_key)
    wasm_hash = scval.to_native(get_return_value(response))
    response_deploy = build_and_send_transaction(
        account,
        lambda builder: builder.append_create_contract_op(
            wasm_id=wasm_hash, address=source_keypair.public_key
        ),
    )
    contract_address = scval.to_native(get_return_value(response_deploy))
    print(contract_address.address)
```

```go Go
func deployContract(ctx context.Context, response protocol.GetTransactionResponse) error {
  account, err := server.LoadAccount(ctx, sourceKeypair.Address())
  if err != nil {
    return err
  }
  returnValue, err := getReturnValue(response)
  if err != nil {
    return err
  }
  wasmHashBytes, ok := returnValue.GetBytes()
  if !ok || len(wasmHashBytes) != 32 {
    return errors.New("upload did not return a Wasm hash")
  }
  var wasmHash xdr.Hash
  copy(wasmHash[:], wasmHashBytes)

  // A random salt, as createCustomContract uses in JavaScript
  var salt xdr.Uint256
  if _, err := rand.Read(salt[:]); err != nil {
    return err
  }

  operation := &txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction{
    HostFunction: xdr.HostFunction{
      Type: xdr.HostFunctionTypeHostFunctionTypeCreateContractV2,
      CreateContractV2: &xdr.CreateContractArgsV2{
        ContractIdPreimage: xdr.ContractIdPreimage{
          Type: xdr.ContractIdPreimageTypeContractIdPreimageFromAddress,
          FromAddress: &xdr.ContractIdPreimageFromAddress{
            Address: xdr.ScAddress{
              Type:      xdr.ScAddressTypeScAddressTypeAccount,
              AccountId: xdr.MustAddressPtr(sourceKeypair.Address()),
            },
            Salt: salt,
          },
        },
        Executable: xdr.ContractExecutable{
          Type:     xdr.ContractExecutableTypeContractExecutableWasm,
          WasmHash: &wasmHash,
        },
        ConstructorArgs: []xdr.ScVal{},
      },
    },
    SourceAccount: sourceKeypair.Address(),
  }
  responseDeploy, err := buildAndSendTransaction(ctx, account, operation)
  if err != nil {
    return err
  }
  contractValue, err := getReturnValue(responseDeploy)
  if err != nil {
    return err
  }
  contractAddress, ok := contractValue.GetAddress()
  if !ok || contractAddress.ContractId == nil {
    return errors.New("deploy did not return a contract address")
  }
  fmt.Println(strkey.MustEncode(strkey.VersionByteContract, (*contractAddress.ContractId)[:]))
  return nil
}
```

</CodeGroup>

This function uses the Wasm hash to deploy the contract using the `createCustomContract` stellar operation, which when wrapped in a transaction is sent to the network, generating a contract address. `scValToNative` converts each return value to a JavaScript value: the Wasm hash bytes after the upload, and the contract address string after the deploy. In Python, `append_create_contract_op` adds the same operation, and `scval.to_native` converts the return values: the Wasm hash to `bytes`, and the contract address to an `Address`. In Go, the code builds the same `CreateContractV2` host function by hand, reads the Wasm hash with `GetBytes`, and encodes the contract ID as a `C...` address with `strkey`.

### Building, Signing and Sending the Transaction

Handle the building, signing, and sending of transactions:

<CodeGroup>

```javascript JavaScript
async function buildAndSendTransaction(account, operations) {
  // Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend.
  // prepareTransaction adds the resource fee on top of this inclusion fee.
  const { sorobanInclusionFee } = await server.getFeeStats();
  const MAX_FEE = 100_000; // stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
  const fee = String(Math.min(Number(sorobanInclusionFee.p90), MAX_FEE));

  const transaction = new StellarSDK.TransactionBuilder(account, {
    fee,
    networkPassphrase: StellarSDK.Networks.TESTNET,
  })
    .addOperation(operations)
    .setTimeout(30)
    .build();

  const tx = await server.prepareTransaction(transaction);
  tx.sign(sourceKeypair);

  console.log("Submitting transaction...");
  const sendResponse = await server.sendTransaction(tx);
  console.log(`Transaction hash: ${sendResponse.hash}`);

  // PENDING and DUPLICATE mean the network has the transaction.
  // TRY_AGAIN_LATER and ERROR mean the network did not accept it.
  if (
    sendResponse.status === "TRY_AGAIN_LATER" ||
    sendResponse.status === "ERROR"
  ) {
    throw new Error(`Transaction not accepted: ${sendResponse.status}`);
  }

  console.log("Awaiting confirmation...");
  // Poll getTransaction once a second, for up to 30 attempts
  const response = await server.pollTransaction(sendResponse.hash, {
    attempts: 30,
  });

  // NOT_FOUND after the last attempt means the result is unknown,
  // not that the transaction failed
  if (response.status === "NOT_FOUND") {
    throw new Error("Not confirmed yet. Check again before resending.");
  }

  if (response.status === "SUCCESS") {
    console.log("Transaction successful.");
    return response;
  } else {
    console.log("Transaction failed.");
    throw new Error(`Transaction did not succeed: ${response.status}`);
  }
}
```

```python Python
def build_and_send_transaction(account, add_operation):
    # Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend.
    # prepare_transaction adds the resource fee on top of this inclusion fee.
    MAX_FEE = 100_000  # stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
    fee = min(server.get_fee_stats().soroban_inclusion_fee.p90, MAX_FEE)

    builder = TransactionBuilder(
        source_account=account,
        network_passphrase=Network.TESTNET_NETWORK_PASSPHRASE,
        base_fee=fee,
    )
    add_operation(builder)
    transaction = builder.set_timeout(30).build()

    tx = server.prepare_transaction(transaction)
    tx.sign(source_keypair)

    print("Submitting transaction...")
    send_response = server.send_transaction(tx)
    print(f"Transaction hash: {send_response.hash}")

    # PENDING and DUPLICATE mean the network has the transaction.
    # TRY_AGAIN_LATER and ERROR mean the network did not accept it.
    if send_response.status in (
        SendTransactionStatus.TRY_AGAIN_LATER,
        SendTransactionStatus.ERROR,
    ):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Transaction not accepted: {send_response.status}")

    print("Awaiting confirmation...")
    # Poll get_transaction once a second, for up to 30 attempts
    response = server.poll_transaction(send_response.hash, max_attempts=30)

    # NOT_FOUND after the last attempt means the result is unknown,
    # not that the transaction failed
    if response.status == GetTransactionStatus.NOT_FOUND:
        raise RuntimeError("Not confirmed yet. Check again before resending.")

    if response.status == GetTransactionStatus.SUCCESS:
        print("Transaction successful.")
        return response
    print("Transaction failed.")
    raise RuntimeError(f"Transaction did not succeed: {response.status}")


def get_return_value(response):
    # The contract's return value is in the transaction meta.
    meta = TransactionMeta.from_xdr(response.result_meta_xdr)
    meta_body = meta.v4 or meta.v3
    return meta_body.soroban_meta.return_value
```

```go Go
func buildAndSendTransaction(
  ctx context.Context,
  account txnbuild.Account,
  operation *txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction,
) (protocol.GetTransactionResponse, error) {
  var none protocol.GetTransactionResponse

  // Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend.
  // prepareTransaction adds the resource fee on top of this inclusion fee.
  feeStats, err := server.GetFeeStats(ctx)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  const maxFee = 100_000 // stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
  fee := min(int64(feeStats.SorobanInclusionFee.P90), maxFee)

  tx, err := prepareTransaction(ctx, txnbuild.TransactionParams{
    SourceAccount:        account,
    IncrementSequenceNum: true,
    BaseFee:              fee,
    Preconditions:        txnbuild.Preconditions{TimeBounds: txnbuild.NewTimeout(30)},
    Operations:           []txnbuild.Operation{operation},
  })
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  tx, err = tx.Sign(network.TestNetworkPassphrase, sourceKeypair)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  envelope, err := tx.Base64()
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }

  fmt.Println("Submitting transaction...")
  sendResponse, err := server.SendTransaction(ctx, protocol.SendTransactionRequest{Transaction: envelope})
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  fmt.Printf("Transaction hash: %s\n", sendResponse.Hash)

  // PENDING and DUPLICATE mean the network has the transaction.
  // TRY_AGAIN_LATER and ERROR mean the network did not accept it.
  if sendResponse.Status == "TRY_AGAIN_LATER" || sendResponse.Status == "ERROR" {
    return none, fmt.Errorf("transaction not accepted: %s", sendResponse.Status)
  }

  fmt.Println("Awaiting confirmation...")
  // Poll getTransaction once a second, for up to 30 attempts
  var response protocol.GetTransactionResponse
  for range 30 {
    response, err = server.GetTransaction(ctx, protocol.GetTransactionRequest{Hash: sendResponse.Hash})
    if err != nil {
      return none, err
    }
    if response.Status != protocol.TransactionStatusNotFound {
      break
    }
    time.Sleep(time.Second)
  }

  // NOT_FOUND after the last attempt means the result is unknown,
  // not that the transaction failed
  if response.Status == protocol.TransactionStatusNotFound {
    return none, errors.New("not confirmed yet, check again before resending")
  }

  if response.Status == protocol.TransactionStatusSuccess {
    fmt.Println("Transaction successful.")
    return response, nil
  }
  fmt.Println("Transaction failed.")
  return response, fmt.Errorf("transaction did not succeed: %s", response.Status)
}

// prepareTransaction simulates the transaction, then builds it again with the
// simulated resources, resource fee, and authorization entries.
func prepareTransaction(ctx context.Context, params txnbuild.TransactionParams) (*txnbuild.Transaction, error) {
  tx, err := txnbuild.NewTransaction(params)
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  envelope, err := tx.Base64()
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  sim, err := server.SimulateTransaction(ctx, protocol.SimulateTransactionRequest{Transaction: envelope})
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  if sim.Error != "" {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("simulation failed: %s", sim.Error)
  }

  var sorobanData xdr.SorobanTransactionData
  if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(sim.TransactionDataXDR, &sorobanData); err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  operation := params.Operations[0].(*txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction)
  operation.Ext = xdr.TransactionExt{V: 1, SorobanData: &sorobanData}

  // Keep the operation's own auth entries; otherwise use the simulated ones.
  if len(operation.Auth) == 0 && len(sim.Results) > 0 && sim.Results[0].AuthXDR != nil {
    for _, entryXDR := range *sim.Results[0].AuthXDR {
      var entry xdr.SorobanAuthorizationEntry
      if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(entryXDR, &entry); err != nil {
        return nil, err
      }
      operation.Auth = append(operation.Auth, entry)
    }
  }

  // Build again with the same sequence number.
  source := tx.SourceAccount()
  params.SourceAccount = &source
  params.IncrementSequenceNum = false
  return txnbuild.NewTransaction(params)
}

func getReturnValue(response protocol.GetTransactionResponse) (xdr.ScVal, error) {
  // The contract's return value is in the transaction meta.
  var meta xdr.TransactionMeta
  if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(response.ResultMetaXDR, &meta); err != nil {
    return xdr.ScVal{}, err
  }
  switch {
  case meta.V4 != nil && meta.V4.SorobanMeta != nil && meta.V4.SorobanMeta.ReturnValue != nil:
    return *meta.V4.SorobanMeta.ReturnValue, nil
  case meta.V3 != nil && meta.V3.SorobanMeta != nil:
    return meta.V3.SorobanMeta.ReturnValue, nil
  }
  return xdr.ScVal{}, errors.New("no return value in the transaction meta")
}
```

</CodeGroup>

This function constructs a transaction, signs it, and submits it to the network. It checks the `sendTransaction` status first: `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` and `ERROR` mean the network did not accept the transaction, so the function stops with an error. Then `server.pollTransaction` waits for the result and stops after 30 attempts, so the script never hangs. If the attempts run out, the status is still `NOT_FOUND`. That means the result is unknown, not that the transaction failed, so check again before you resend it. [Submit a transaction and wait](/docs/build/guides/transactions/submit-transaction-wait) shows the full handling. For the SDK's own flow, read its [Invoke a Contract guide](https://stellar.github.io/js-stellar-sdk/guides/06-invoke-a-contract/).

The Python version also defines `get_return_value`. The Python SDK's response has no return value field, so the helper reads it from the transaction meta in `result_meta_xdr`. The Go version does the same with `getReturnValue` and `ResultMetaXDR`. The Go SDK has no `prepareTransaction`, so the Go version defines one: it simulates the transaction, then adds the simulated resources, resource fee, and authorization entries.

## Running the Script

Execute the deployment script:

<CodeGroup>

```javascript JavaScript
const server = new StellarSDK.rpc.Server(
  "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org:443",
);
const sourceKeypair = StellarSDK.Keypair.fromSecret("Your_Secret_Key");
const wasmFilePath =
  "../hello-world/target/wasm32v1-none/release/hello_world.wasm"; // Adjust this path as necessary

try {
  let uploadResponse = await uploadWasm(wasmFilePath);
  await deployContract(uploadResponse);
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error);
}
```

```python Python
server = SorobanServer("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org:443")
source_keypair = Keypair.from_secret("Your_Secret_Key")
# Adjust this path as necessary
wasm_file_path = "../hello-world/target/wasm32v1-none/release/hello_world.wasm"

try:
    upload_response = upload_wasm(wasm_file_path)
    deploy_contract(upload_response)
except Exception as error:
    print(error)
```

```go Go
var server = client.NewClient("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org:443", nil)
var sourceKeypair = keypair.MustParseFull("Your_Secret_Key")

// Adjust this path as necessary
const wasmFilePath = "../hello-world/target/wasm32v1-none/release/hello_world.wasm"

func main() {
  ctx := context.Background()
  uploadResponse, err := uploadWasm(ctx, wasmFilePath)
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  if err := deployContract(ctx, uploadResponse); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
}
```

</CodeGroup>

Replace "Your_Secret_Key" with your actual secret key. This script initiates the upload of the Wasm file and deploys the contract, resulting in a contract address where the contract is deployed. Run the Go version with `go run main.go`.

This is just demo code, so ensure that you handle secrets and private keys securely in production environments and never expose them in your code repositories. This guide should provide you with a clear path to installing and deploying your smart contracts using JavaScript, Python, or Go code.

## Complete Script

Here are all the snippets stacked together in a single file for convenience:

<CodeGroup>

```javascript JavaScript
import * as StellarSDK from "@stellar/stellar-sdk";
import fs from "fs";
async function uploadWasm(filePath) {
  const bytecode = fs.readFileSync(filePath);
  const account = await server.getAccount(sourceKeypair.publicKey());
  const operation = StellarSDK.Operation.uploadContractWasm({ wasm: bytecode });
  return await buildAndSendTransaction(account, operation);
}
async function deployContract(response) {
  const account = await server.getAccount(sourceKeypair.publicKey());
  const operation = StellarSDK.Operation.createCustomContract({
    wasmHash: StellarSDK.scValToNative(response.returnValue),
    address: StellarSDK.Address.fromString(sourceKeypair.publicKey()),
  });
  const responseDeploy = await buildAndSendTransaction(account, operation);
  const contractAddress = StellarSDK.scValToNative(responseDeploy.returnValue);
  console.log(contractAddress);
}
async function buildAndSendTransaction(account, operations) {
  // Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend.
  // prepareTransaction adds the resource fee on top of this inclusion fee.
  const { sorobanInclusionFee } = await server.getFeeStats();
  const MAX_FEE = 100_000; // stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
  const fee = String(Math.min(Number(sorobanInclusionFee.p90), MAX_FEE));

  const transaction = new StellarSDK.TransactionBuilder(account, {
    fee,
    networkPassphrase: StellarSDK.Networks.TESTNET,
  })
    .addOperation(operations)
    .setTimeout(30)
    .build();

  const tx = await server.prepareTransaction(transaction);
  tx.sign(sourceKeypair);

  console.log("Submitting transaction...");
  const sendResponse = await server.sendTransaction(tx);
  console.log(`Transaction hash: ${sendResponse.hash}`);

  // PENDING and DUPLICATE mean the network has the transaction.
  // TRY_AGAIN_LATER and ERROR mean the network did not accept it.
  if (
    sendResponse.status === "TRY_AGAIN_LATER" ||
    sendResponse.status === "ERROR"
  ) {
    throw new Error(`Transaction not accepted: ${sendResponse.status}`);
  }

  console.log("Awaiting confirmation...");
  // Poll getTransaction once a second, for up to 30 attempts
  const response = await server.pollTransaction(sendResponse.hash, {
    attempts: 30,
  });

  // NOT_FOUND after the last attempt means the result is unknown,
  // not that the transaction failed
  if (response.status === "NOT_FOUND") {
    throw new Error("Not confirmed yet. Check again before resending.");
  }

  if (response.status === "SUCCESS") {
    console.log("Transaction successful.");
    return response;
  } else {
    console.log("Transaction failed.");
    throw new Error(`Transaction did not succeed: ${response.status}`);
  }
}

const server = new StellarSDK.rpc.Server(
  "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org:443",
);
const sourceKeypair = StellarSDK.Keypair.fromSecret("Your_Secret_Key");
const wasmFilePath =
  "../hello-world/target/wasm32v1-none/release/hello_world.wasm"; // Adjust this path as necessary

try {
  let uploadResponse = await uploadWasm(wasmFilePath);
  await deployContract(uploadResponse);
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error);
}
```

```python Python
from stellar_sdk import Keypair, Network, SorobanServer, TransactionBuilder, scval
from stellar_sdk.soroban_rpc import GetTransactionStatus, SendTransactionStatus
from stellar_sdk.xdr import TransactionMeta


def upload_wasm(file_path):
    with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
        bytecode = f.read()
    account = server.load_account(source_keypair.public_key)
    return build_and_send_transaction(
        account, lambda builder: builder.append_upload_contract_wasm_op(bytecode)
    )


def deploy_contract(response):
    account = server.load_account(source_keypair.public_key)
    wasm_hash = scval.to_native(get_return_value(response))
    response_deploy = build_and_send_transaction(
        account,
        lambda builder: builder.append_create_contract_op(
            wasm_id=wasm_hash, address=source_keypair.public_key
        ),
    )
    contract_address = scval.to_native(get_return_value(response_deploy))
    print(contract_address.address)


def build_and_send_transaction(account, add_operation):
    # Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend.
    # prepare_transaction adds the resource fee on top of this inclusion fee.
    MAX_FEE = 100_000  # stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
    fee = min(server.get_fee_stats().soroban_inclusion_fee.p90, MAX_FEE)

    builder = TransactionBuilder(
        source_account=account,
        network_passphrase=Network.TESTNET_NETWORK_PASSPHRASE,
        base_fee=fee,
    )
    add_operation(builder)
    transaction = builder.set_timeout(30).build()

    tx = server.prepare_transaction(transaction)
    tx.sign(source_keypair)

    print("Submitting transaction...")
    send_response = server.send_transaction(tx)
    print(f"Transaction hash: {send_response.hash}")

    # PENDING and DUPLICATE mean the network has the transaction.
    # TRY_AGAIN_LATER and ERROR mean the network did not accept it.
    if send_response.status in (
        SendTransactionStatus.TRY_AGAIN_LATER,
        SendTransactionStatus.ERROR,
    ):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Transaction not accepted: {send_response.status}")

    print("Awaiting confirmation...")
    # Poll get_transaction once a second, for up to 30 attempts
    response = server.poll_transaction(send_response.hash, max_attempts=30)

    # NOT_FOUND after the last attempt means the result is unknown,
    # not that the transaction failed
    if response.status == GetTransactionStatus.NOT_FOUND:
        raise RuntimeError("Not confirmed yet. Check again before resending.")

    if response.status == GetTransactionStatus.SUCCESS:
        print("Transaction successful.")
        return response
    print("Transaction failed.")
    raise RuntimeError(f"Transaction did not succeed: {response.status}")


def get_return_value(response):
    # The contract's return value is in the transaction meta.
    meta = TransactionMeta.from_xdr(response.result_meta_xdr)
    meta_body = meta.v4 or meta.v3
    return meta_body.soroban_meta.return_value


server = SorobanServer("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org:443")
source_keypair = Keypair.from_secret("Your_Secret_Key")
# Adjust this path as necessary
wasm_file_path = "../hello-world/target/wasm32v1-none/release/hello_world.wasm"

try:
    upload_response = upload_wasm(wasm_file_path)
    deploy_contract(upload_response)
except Exception as error:
    print(error)
```

```go Go
package main

import (
  "context"
  "crypto/rand"
  "errors"
  "fmt"
  "log"
  "os"
  "time"

  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/keypair"
  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/network"
  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/strkey"
  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/txnbuild"
  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/xdr"

  client "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/clients/rpcclient"
  protocol "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/protocols/rpc"
)

func uploadWasm(ctx context.Context, filePath string) (protocol.GetTransactionResponse, error) {
  bytecode, err := os.ReadFile(filePath)
  if err != nil {
    return protocol.GetTransactionResponse{}, err
  }
  account, err := server.LoadAccount(ctx, sourceKeypair.Address())
  if err != nil {
    return protocol.GetTransactionResponse{}, err
  }
  operation := &txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction{
    HostFunction: xdr.HostFunction{
      Type: xdr.HostFunctionTypeHostFunctionTypeUploadContractWasm,
      Wasm: &bytecode,
    },
    SourceAccount: sourceKeypair.Address(),
  }
  return buildAndSendTransaction(ctx, account, operation)
}

func deployContract(ctx context.Context, response protocol.GetTransactionResponse) error {
  account, err := server.LoadAccount(ctx, sourceKeypair.Address())
  if err != nil {
    return err
  }
  returnValue, err := getReturnValue(response)
  if err != nil {
    return err
  }
  wasmHashBytes, ok := returnValue.GetBytes()
  if !ok || len(wasmHashBytes) != 32 {
    return errors.New("upload did not return a Wasm hash")
  }
  var wasmHash xdr.Hash
  copy(wasmHash[:], wasmHashBytes)

  // A random salt, as createCustomContract uses in JavaScript
  var salt xdr.Uint256
  if _, err := rand.Read(salt[:]); err != nil {
    return err
  }

  operation := &txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction{
    HostFunction: xdr.HostFunction{
      Type: xdr.HostFunctionTypeHostFunctionTypeCreateContractV2,
      CreateContractV2: &xdr.CreateContractArgsV2{
        ContractIdPreimage: xdr.ContractIdPreimage{
          Type: xdr.ContractIdPreimageTypeContractIdPreimageFromAddress,
          FromAddress: &xdr.ContractIdPreimageFromAddress{
            Address: xdr.ScAddress{
              Type:      xdr.ScAddressTypeScAddressTypeAccount,
              AccountId: xdr.MustAddressPtr(sourceKeypair.Address()),
            },
            Salt: salt,
          },
        },
        Executable: xdr.ContractExecutable{
          Type:     xdr.ContractExecutableTypeContractExecutableWasm,
          WasmHash: &wasmHash,
        },
        ConstructorArgs: []xdr.ScVal{},
      },
    },
    SourceAccount: sourceKeypair.Address(),
  }
  responseDeploy, err := buildAndSendTransaction(ctx, account, operation)
  if err != nil {
    return err
  }
  contractValue, err := getReturnValue(responseDeploy)
  if err != nil {
    return err
  }
  contractAddress, ok := contractValue.GetAddress()
  if !ok || contractAddress.ContractId == nil {
    return errors.New("deploy did not return a contract address")
  }
  fmt.Println(strkey.MustEncode(strkey.VersionByteContract, (*contractAddress.ContractId)[:]))
  return nil
}

func buildAndSendTransaction(
  ctx context.Context,
  account txnbuild.Account,
  operation *txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction,
) (protocol.GetTransactionResponse, error) {
  var none protocol.GetTransactionResponse

  // Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend.
  // prepareTransaction adds the resource fee on top of this inclusion fee.
  feeStats, err := server.GetFeeStats(ctx)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  const maxFee = 100_000 // stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
  fee := min(int64(feeStats.SorobanInclusionFee.P90), maxFee)

  tx, err := prepareTransaction(ctx, txnbuild.TransactionParams{
    SourceAccount:        account,
    IncrementSequenceNum: true,
    BaseFee:              fee,
    Preconditions:        txnbuild.Preconditions{TimeBounds: txnbuild.NewTimeout(30)},
    Operations:           []txnbuild.Operation{operation},
  })
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  tx, err = tx.Sign(network.TestNetworkPassphrase, sourceKeypair)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  envelope, err := tx.Base64()
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }

  fmt.Println("Submitting transaction...")
  sendResponse, err := server.SendTransaction(ctx, protocol.SendTransactionRequest{Transaction: envelope})
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  fmt.Printf("Transaction hash: %s\n", sendResponse.Hash)

  // PENDING and DUPLICATE mean the network has the transaction.
  // TRY_AGAIN_LATER and ERROR mean the network did not accept it.
  if sendResponse.Status == "TRY_AGAIN_LATER" || sendResponse.Status == "ERROR" {
    return none, fmt.Errorf("transaction not accepted: %s", sendResponse.Status)
  }

  fmt.Println("Awaiting confirmation...")
  // Poll getTransaction once a second, for up to 30 attempts
  var response protocol.GetTransactionResponse
  for range 30 {
    response, err = server.GetTransaction(ctx, protocol.GetTransactionRequest{Hash: sendResponse.Hash})
    if err != nil {
      return none, err
    }
    if response.Status != protocol.TransactionStatusNotFound {
      break
    }
    time.Sleep(time.Second)
  }

  // NOT_FOUND after the last attempt means the result is unknown,
  // not that the transaction failed
  if response.Status == protocol.TransactionStatusNotFound {
    return none, errors.New("not confirmed yet, check again before resending")
  }

  if response.Status == protocol.TransactionStatusSuccess {
    fmt.Println("Transaction successful.")
    return response, nil
  }
  fmt.Println("Transaction failed.")
  return response, fmt.Errorf("transaction did not succeed: %s", response.Status)
}

// prepareTransaction simulates the transaction, then builds it again with the
// simulated resources, resource fee, and authorization entries.
func prepareTransaction(ctx context.Context, params txnbuild.TransactionParams) (*txnbuild.Transaction, error) {
  tx, err := txnbuild.NewTransaction(params)
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  envelope, err := tx.Base64()
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  sim, err := server.SimulateTransaction(ctx, protocol.SimulateTransactionRequest{Transaction: envelope})
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  if sim.Error != "" {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("simulation failed: %s", sim.Error)
  }

  var sorobanData xdr.SorobanTransactionData
  if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(sim.TransactionDataXDR, &sorobanData); err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  operation := params.Operations[0].(*txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction)
  operation.Ext = xdr.TransactionExt{V: 1, SorobanData: &sorobanData}

  // Keep the operation's own auth entries; otherwise use the simulated ones.
  if len(operation.Auth) == 0 && len(sim.Results) > 0 && sim.Results[0].AuthXDR != nil {
    for _, entryXDR := range *sim.Results[0].AuthXDR {
      var entry xdr.SorobanAuthorizationEntry
      if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(entryXDR, &entry); err != nil {
        return nil, err
      }
      operation.Auth = append(operation.Auth, entry)
    }
  }

  // Build again with the same sequence number.
  source := tx.SourceAccount()
  params.SourceAccount = &source
  params.IncrementSequenceNum = false
  return txnbuild.NewTransaction(params)
}

func getReturnValue(response protocol.GetTransactionResponse) (xdr.ScVal, error) {
  // The contract's return value is in the transaction meta.
  var meta xdr.TransactionMeta
  if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(response.ResultMetaXDR, &meta); err != nil {
    return xdr.ScVal{}, err
  }
  switch {
  case meta.V4 != nil && meta.V4.SorobanMeta != nil && meta.V4.SorobanMeta.ReturnValue != nil:
    return *meta.V4.SorobanMeta.ReturnValue, nil
  case meta.V3 != nil && meta.V3.SorobanMeta != nil:
    return meta.V3.SorobanMeta.ReturnValue, nil
  }
  return xdr.ScVal{}, errors.New("no return value in the transaction meta")
}

var server = client.NewClient("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org:443", nil)
var sourceKeypair = keypair.MustParseFull("Your_Secret_Key")

// Adjust this path as necessary
const wasmFilePath = "../hello-world/target/wasm32v1-none/release/hello_world.wasm"

func main() {
  ctx := context.Background()
  uploadResponse, err := uploadWasm(ctx, wasmFilePath)
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
  if err := deployContract(ctx, uploadResponse); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
  }
}
```
